clue.text: Sunless weeks perhaps this old poet's woe!

wordplay.note: a week with its Sunday taken away is one day short, and the phrase describes that shortfall, split 4,1,3

explanation.surface: A poet laments a run of grey, sunless weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunless' tempts you towards weather, but it means weeks missing their Sunday: they lack a day, split 4,1,3.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic exclamation of sorrow or regret, found mainly in older poetry.

explanation.definitionFit: Lights is the setters' term for the entries that fill a crossword grid.

clue.text: Recorder turned up with academician

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, to come
a member of the Royal Academy is a Royal Academician, RA

explanation.surface: A recording device is flipped over beside an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' looks like a reversal, but it simply means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera records images, so it is a recording device.

clue.text: Fighting group losing its leader

indicators.note: the first letter, at the head of the word, is dropped

parts.note: a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: A rebel militia is left leaderless.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers in action are in battle, engaged in combat.

clue.text: Aforementioned morning post baker opens before getting up

indicators.note: the combination opens up the other word and sits inside it

parts.note: before getting up in the morning you are still abed

indicators.note: post means after, so the morning goes after the baker

parts.note: an oven bakes

explanation.surface: A baker posts loaves early, opening shop before the rest are up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning post' looks like the newspaper or first delivery, but 'post' is Latin for after.
explanation.definitionFit: Above-named means mentioned earlier in the same document.

clue.text: Dodge blockades on riot

definitions.note: a riot, like a scream, is something or someone hilarious

indicators.note: to blockade is to surround and shut in, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a dodge is a scam, a swindle
RE means 'on the subject of'

explanation.surface: Police use a ruse to block off a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a very funny person or thing is called both a riot and a scream.

clue.text: Big city that was upset at a cult procuring clubs

definitions.note: the city's former name, now Kolkata

indicators.note: to procure is to obtain, so the jumble takes in the card suit
upset means overturned and jumbled

parts.note: letters taken as written
C is the card-suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A city disturbed by a cult that recruits gangs armed with clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian metropolis officially became Kolkata in 2001, so the old name belongs to the past.

clue.text: What I'd like to be is oldie, wizened with age

indicators.note: wizened means shrivelled and twisted, so these letters are contorted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrinkled pensioner wishes to be young again.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis the ego ideal is the self one aspires to become.

clue.text: Official sauce, and what it does for topping

parts.note: mayo is mayonnaise

indicators.note: topping means cutting the top off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a sauce dresses a salad

explanation.surface: A salad cream and how it serves as a topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like a garnish, but it means beheading the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is a female mayor or a mayor's wife, a civic dignitary.

clue.text: One of the men in white coats worked on it with good sense

parts.words: One of the men in white coats
parts.note: cricket umpires wear white coats; UMP is short for umpire

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A psychiatric orderly handles a job sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men in white coats' suggests asylum attendants, but these are cricket umpires, whose long white coats are traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is practical common sense and initiative.

clue.text: Cruel individual takes look inside

indicators.note: the first word takes in the second
says where the second word goes: into the middle of the first

parts.note: a body is a person, as in 'a nice old body'
LO is the old word for 'look!'

explanation.surface: A cruel person has a good look round inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloody can mean bloodthirsty or savage, as in a bloody tyrant.

clue.text: Go through apple pie?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to leaf through pages or papers when searching them
second meaning: a folded fruit pastry; the question mark marks apple as an example of the filling

explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase is read as a two-word phrase, the pastry as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple turnover is a pastry, and to turn over a pile of papers is to search through them.

clue.text: Crows gathering on the counter would be 10 odd

indicators.note: read on the counter means read counter to the usual direction, backwards

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, bloody, is a synonym of red
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.walkthrough: RED RUM, famous as a Grand National horse and the reversed word in The Shining, gives the answer backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a flock of crows is a murder.

clue.text: Sixty could be right for the cryptic crossword compiler!

wordplay.words: could be right for the cryptic crossword compiler
wordplay.note: split 5,1,4; the middle of 'three' is R, a setter's way to clue right

explanation.surface: A setter wonders if sixty is the right number of clues.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, split differently, is itself a cryptic instruction giving R, the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty.

clue.text: Cocktails chap hasn't drunk, which stifles cheers!

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the jumble closes round the next part
drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters taken as written for the jumble
TA is British for thanks; cheers is used the same way

explanation.surface: A teetotal chap smothers his toasts while others order cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a whiskey and vermouth cocktail, named after the New York borough.

clue.text: Gave cheer when solvers are introduced to new girl?

wordplay.words: when solvers are introduced to new girl?
wordplay.note: a deb, a girl new to society, has you, the solvers, put inside; the result written up, as a down entry reverses, is the answer split 6,2

explanation.surface: Solvers are cheered on meeting a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction: the first word written UP, as a down entry is reversed, gives DEB around YOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyed up means lifted the spirits of, encouraged.

clue.text: The last Number One Gloria Gaynor initiated

parts.note: Gloria Swanson, star of Sunset Boulevard, is one Gloria

indicators.note: to initiate is to begin, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the singer's surname, whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: Gloria Gaynor's final chart-topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number One' reads as a chart hit, but the definition stops at 'Number', a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final performance, as the dying swan is said to sing once.

clue.text: Contest's decisive point, after which head completely drops in court

indicators.note: the shifted word goes inside the courting word

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: the head letter falls all the way to the end of the word

parts.note: later means after

explanation.surface: After a decisive moment in a match, a head falls in court.

clue.text: Neat bachelor eclipses each one of fashion model's exes

indicators.note: to eclipse is to obscure by covering, so the first part surrounds the rest

parts.note: a bachelor is unwed
Ken was the boyfriend of Barbie, the fashion doll; they split in 2004

explanation.surface: A tidy single man outshines all of a model's former partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is spirits taken undiluted. The fashion model is the doll Barbie.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat drink is undiluted, served without water or mixer, so its strength is not reduced.

clue.text: For sleigh-riders from the south, not very useful direction finders

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means from the bottom up
not means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: satnavs are car navigation systems

explanation.surface: Satnavs are no use to those riding sleighs from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas figures ride sleighs pulled by reindeer.

clue.text: Not at all dry for one left in French city

indicators.note: the dry letters stand for, replacing, one letter

parts.note: Lille is a city in northern France
one of the letters standing for left
TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: A French city where nowhere is dry and one person was left.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, little means not at all, as in 'little did they suspect'.

clue.text: " Telegraph cryptic shakes 'enigmatic' tag" — PA

indicators.note: to shake off something is to be rid of it, so letters are removed

parts.note: the paper's name made cryptic, its nine letters scrambled into this order
a puzzling, jumbled tag: its three letters in any order, here as they sit to be removed

clue.text: Returns from this bet? I'm afraid not!

clue.text: At a function collecting trinketry

parts.note: taken as written, the single letter

indicators.note: the function word gathers the cheap goods into its middle

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
tat is cheap, tasteless ornaments

explanation.surface: Someone gathers knick-knacks at a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening word looks like a mere preposition, but it is the definition: the symbol of element 85.

clue.text: Idly draw benefit, stretched by overdraft

indicators.note: the word is stretched to fit the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests drawing money, but it means sketching.

clue.text: On reverse, image's extremely strong impression

too means excessively

explanation.definitionFit: A footstep can be a footprint, the mark a foot leaves pressed in the ground.

clue.text: Time to put an end to monster affair

definitions.note: as in 'not my pigeon', meaning not my concern

indicators.note: the time word is put on the end of the monster word

parts.note: a pig is a greedy brute, a monster of appetite
an eon is an immeasurably long time

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is time to end a monstrous love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests romance, but it is business or concern, as in the British idiom 'that's not my pigeon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon is an informal word for a person's concern or responsibility, from an old spelling of pidgin.

clue.text: Dons don it, tailors tailor it … and troopers do what troopers do!

definitions.text: Dons don it, tailors tailor it
definitions.note: clothing for men, worn by dons (who don it) and cut by tailors

parts.note: troopers are soldiers, men
to swear like a trooper is to curse heavily

explanation.surface: A playful run of puns: what academics wear, what tailors cut, and how soldiers talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' are Oxbridge academics who also put it on; the troopers come from the idiom 'swear like a trooper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is clothing for men, which dons wear and tailors make.
